points.text: an entry's `frontend` module runs in the browser (and in Electron unless a `frontendElectron` module is given), and its `backend` module runs in Node.js (and in Electron unless a `backendElectron` module is given)
points.check: Doc: packages/core/README.md L41-46 ('`frontend` is used in the browser env and as well in the electron if `frontendElectron` is not provided'; '`backend` is used in the node env and as well in the electron env if `backendElectron` is not provided'). Code (author's pointers, for the re-checker): dev-packages/application-package/src/application-package.ts L161-162 (frontendElectronModules = computeModules('frontendElectron', 'frontend')) and L277; the code also knows keys the README doesn't list (frontendOnly, frontendPreload, preload, secondaryWindow in packages/core and packages/terminal).
points.note: Doc: packages/core/README.md L41-46 (frontend in the browser and in Electron unless frontendElectron is given; backend in node and in Electron unless backendElectron is given). Code: dev-packages/application-package/src/application-package.ts L161-162 (computeModules('frontendElectron', 'frontend')), L173-174 (computeModules('backendElectron', 'backend')), L192 (the fallback is per entry), L270-277 (target modules picked by target). The code knows more keys than the README (frontendOnly, frontendPreload, preload, secondaryWindow, electronMain; extension-package.ts L22-33); immaterial. In scope.

points.text: inside a package, code is split into platform folders that limit what it may use: `common` (runs everywhere), `browser` and `browser-only` (DOM), `node` (Node.js), and `electron-browser`, `electron-node` and `electron-main` for Electron; `browser` and `node` may use only `common`
points.check: Doc: doc/code-organization.md L3-17 (common, browser, browser-only, node, electron-node, electron-browser and electron-main, each with the folders it 'May use code from'). Code (author's pointers, for the re-checker): packages/core/src holds browser, browser-only, common, electron-browser, electron-common, electron-main, electron-node and node (electron-common isn't in the doc); theiaExtensions paths follow the folders (lib/browser/..., lib/node/..., lib/electron-browser/...); dev-packages/private-eslint-plugin/rules/runtime-import-check.js.
points.note: Doc: doc/code-organization.md L3-17 (common; browser, browser-only and node may use common only; electron-node, electron-browser, electron-main with their allowances). Code: packages/core/src holds browser, browser-only, common, electron-browser, electron-common, electron-main, electron-node, node; dev-packages/private-eslint-plugin/rules/runtime-import-check.js L57-63 (browser -> [common], node -> [common]). The code also has electron-common, which the doc and the point don't list, and the lint rule lets electron-main import electron-common/node/common rather than the doc's electron-node; neither touches the point's claims. In scope, though peripheral (it is how a package keeps frontend and backend code apart).

points.text: an application is configured under `theia` in its `package.json`: its target, `browser` (the default) or `electron`, and frontend and backend settings such as the application name and default preferences

By default `browser` target is used'). Code (author's pointers, for the re-checker): examples/browser/package.json theia (frontend.config.applicationName and preferences, backend.config; no target) and examples/electron/package.json theia.target 'electron'.
points.note: Doc: dev-packages/cli/README.md L68 (configured via the `theia` property in package.json), L72-101 (applicationName, default preferences), L120 ('The following targets are supported: `browser` and `electron`. points.text: the CLI generates the application's frontend and backend code and its esbuild configuration; `theia build` bundles it and `theia start` runs the backend server (on localhost:3000 for the browser target), and in Electron the generated `electron-main` script forks the backend into a Node.js subprocess
